---
applyTo: "android/feature-financial/**"
---

# feature-financial module instructions

## Purpose and scope

- `android/feature-financial` is the finance feature library used only by the `:app` application module. It owns the financial home screen, the new-transaction flow, and all transaction/card/transaction-category data access.
- It is an Android library without product flavors. Build and test it with `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-financial:compileDebugKotlin` and `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-financial:testDebugUnitTest`.

## Structure

- Kotlin packages stay under `com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp...` (matching `:app`) even though the Gradle namespace is `com.vfdeginformatica.feature.financial`. Do not change package names when adding or moving files; app-side DI, imports, and navigation depend on them.
- Follow the repository-wide layering inside this module:
  - `data/remote/datasource` — Firestore DAOs (`TransactionDao`, `CardDao`, `CategoryTransactionDao`) and their `*Impl` classes receiving `FirebaseFirestore` via constructor.
  - `data/remote/dto` — Firestore DTOs (`TransactionDto`, `CardDto`, `CategoryTransactionDto`).
  - `data/remote/repository` — repository implementations wrapping DAOs.
  - `data/mapper` — explicit DTO↔domain conversions (`TransactionMapper`); never expose DTOs to presentation code.
  - `domain/model`, `domain/repository`, `domain/use_case/financial/...` — models, repository interfaces, and use cases returning `Flow<Resource<T>>`.
  - `presentation/screen/<screen>` — `*Route.kt` (navigation/composition), `*Screen.kt` (UI), `*ViewModel.kt` (behavior), and `contract/` with `UiState`, `Event`, `Effect` types.
  - `presentation/common` — shared UI helpers: `FinancialFormatters` (`formatCurrency`, `monthLabel`, `formatDate` dd/MM/yyyy, plus the color helpers `incomeColor`, `expenseColor` and `balanceColor(balance)`), `CurrencyVisualTransformation`, `DateField` + `FinancialDatePickerDialog` (read-only tappable date field + Material3 `DatePickerDialog`), `FinancialDates.toTransactionTimestamp()` and the transaction edit dialogs.

## Color convention

- Plain expense amounts (month list items, "Despesas" totals, invoice totals/items, breakdown cards, category icons, the "Gasto" FAB) use a **neutral** color (`expenseColor` = `onSurface`, or `onSurfaceVariant`/`secondaryContainer` for icons/FAB). Do not paint expenses red.
- `colorScheme.error` (red) is reserved for **negative balances** (`balanceColor`), error messages and destructive actions (Excluir). Incomes and non-negative balances use `incomeColor` (green).

## Dependencies and wiring

- The module depends on `:feature-qrcode` only for shared infrastructure: the `common.Resource` wrapper and the `AppScaffold` composable. Do not add QR business logic dependencies; if more shared pieces are needed, prefer extracting a `:core` module.
- Hilt wiring is app-local: `android/app/di/DaoModule.kt` and `RepositoryModule.kt` provide the DAOs and repositories implemented here. When adding a new DAO/repository, add the corresponding `@Provides` bindings in `android/app/di`, not in this module.
- Navigation routes for this module's screens (`financial_screen`, `new_transaction_screen/{transactionType}`, `new_card_screen`, `card_list_screen`, `card_detail_screen/{cardId}`, `category_list_screen`, `category_detail_screen?categoryId={categoryId}`) are declared in the shared `Screen` sealed class and composed into the nav graph in `android/app` (`MySuperApp.kt`). New screens need a route there plus a `composable(...)` entry in the app nav graph.

## Domain model (validated against the app flow)

- A transaction is either **INCOME (Receita)** or **EXPENSE (Despesa/Gasto)** (`TransactionType`), chosen before opening the form. The dashboard's `TransactionFabMenu` expands the main FAB into two extended FAB actions, "Gasto" and "Receita"; choosing one closes the menu and navigates with the required `transactionType` argument. The close FAB or system Back collapses the menu. `AppScaffold.floatingActionButtonContent` allows this custom FAB without changing other screens' FAB behavior.
  - `NewTransactionViewModel` reads the required type from `SavedStateHandle` using `Screen.NewTransactionScreen.TRANSACTION_TYPE`. The type stays fixed for that form, including after card creation/reload or navigation state restoration. There is no TypeChanged event or type selector in the form; the toolbar identifies it as "Novo gasto" or "Nova receita".
  - **INCOME**: title, amount, optional description, the destination card, and an optional "Receita recorrente" switch (e.g. salary) used by the projection tab. All cards are selectable (credit-only included); `allowsDeposit` no longer restricts the list. A card is required and no payment method is chosen.
  - **EXPENSE**: title, amount, optional description, a required card, a payment method (`DEBIT`/`CREDIT`) constrained by the card's `paymentMethods`, and multi-select categories. When the method is `CREDIT`, the user picks either a number of installments (1–12 or 24) or "Compra Recorrente" (`isRecurring = true`). When the method is `DEBIT`, a "Compra recorrente" switch is available instead. Switching card or payment method resets `isRecurring`. The payment-method section is rendered only for EXPENSE — INCOME picks just the destination card. Category chips are shown for both types, filtered to categories whose `transactionType` matches the selected type.
- `installments` is persisted only for non-recurring CREDIT expenses; otherwise it is `null`.
- Amount fields (new transaction and the edit dialog) use a cents-based currency mask: UI state holds only digits representing centavos (e.g. `"12480"` = R$ 124,80), rendered by `presentation/common/CurrencyVisualTransformation`. Convert with `CurrencyVisualTransformation.centsToDouble` before persisting — Firestore stores plain `Double` reais.
- `CardDto` (`cards` collection): `bank`, `finalCode`, `paymentMethods` (list of `DEBIT`/`CREDIT`), `invoiceDueDate`, `allowsDeposit`, `closingDay` (invoice closing day; `0` means "no closing day configured"). Cards can be created in-app via the `new_card` screen (reached from the card dropdown on the new-transaction screen): bank + payment-method chips, plus `finalCode`/`closingDay`/`invoiceDueDate` when CREDIT; `allowsDeposit` is always saved as `true`. Optional "Saldo inicial" and "Fatura atual" values are persisted as regular transactions (INCOME, and EXPENSE/CREDIT with computed `invoiceMonth`, respectively) so they show up in the dashboard/projection and stay editable through the edit dialog.
- Card management screens: the drawer's "Controle Financeiro" entry expands into "Dashboard" (FinancialScreen), "Cartões" (`card_list` screen) and "Categorias" (`category_list` screen). The card list navigates to the `card_detail` screen (`card_detail_screen/{cardId}` route, cardId read via `SavedStateHandle`), which edits `bank`/`paymentMethods`/`finalCode`/`closingDay`/`invoiceDueDate` through `UpdateCardUseCase` and has an "Adicionar saldo" section that creates an INCOME transaction ("Ajuste de saldo — {bank}") via `NewTransactionUseCase` instead of storing balance on the card doc.
- `transactions` documents carry: `title`, `description`, `transactionType` (**required**: `EXPENSE` | `INCOME`), `paymentMethod`, `amount`, `isRecurring`, `transactionDate`, `category` (list of category ids), `status`, `cardId`, `invoiceMonth`, `installmentGroupId`, `installments`, `installmentNumber`, and — for recurring docs — `recurrenceStart`, `recurrenceEnd`, `excludedMonths`, `overrides`. `TransactionMapper.toModel()` treats a missing/unknown `transactionType` as `EXPENSE`; `Transaction.toDto()` is the reverse mapping (used by the recurrence split).

### Transaction categories

- Collection `transactions_category/{categoryId}`: `title` (string, required, non-empty), `description` (string, optional, default `""`), `transactionType` (string, required: `EXPENSE` = despesa, `INCOME` = receita). A category belongs to exactly one type.
- Legacy documents created before the field existed are treated as `EXPENSE` by the client (`CategoryTransactionDto.transactionType` defaults to `"EXPENSE"`, and `TransactionCategoryMapper.toTransactionType()` falls back to `EXPENSE` for null/unknown values). Run the backfill script (see "Data") once so the field is physically present.
- Domain model is `domain/model/TransactionCategory` (`id`, `title`, `description`, `type: TransactionType`), converted via `data/mapper/TransactionCategoryMapper.kt` (`toModel()`/`toDto()`). New screens use the domain model; the pre-existing `NewTransactionUiState`/`FinancialUiState` still hold `CategoryTransactionDto` and read `transactionType` from it.
- Management screens:
  - `category_list` (`category_list_screen` route, drawer item "Categorias"): lists categories grouped under "Despesas"/"Receitas" headers, FAB "Nova categoria". Reloads on `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` like `card_list`.
  - `category_detail` (`category_detail_screen?categoryId={categoryId}` route; the `categoryId` nav arg is nullable — absent means "create" mode, present means "edit" mode; read via `SavedStateHandle`, key `CategoryDetailViewModel.CATEGORY_ID_ARG`): type chips (Despesa/Receita), title (required, max 40 chars), description (optional, max 120 chars), Save button, and in edit mode an "Excluir categoria" button guarded by an `AlertDialog`.
- Use cases (`domain/use_case/financial/transaction_category`): `GetTransactionsCategoriesUseCase`, `AddTransactionCategoryUseCase`, `UpdateTransactionCategoryUseCase`, `DeleteTransactionCategoryUseCase`.
- **Deleting a category** (`DeleteTransactionCategoryUseCase`) must never leave orphan ids in `transactions.category`. It first calls `TransactionRepository.removeCategoryFromTransactions(categoryId)` — `whereArrayContains("category", id)` + `WriteBatch` updates with `FieldValue.arrayRemove(id)` in chunks of 500 — and only if that succeeds calls `CategoryTransactionRepository.deleteCategory(id)`. On cleanup failure the category is kept and the user can retry.
- Type-aware category pickers: the new-transaction screen shows categories for **both** INCOME and EXPENSE, filtered by the fixed navigation type (`NewTransactionUiState.categoriesForType`). The dashboard's category filter lists `FinancialUiState.categoriesForFilter` (all categories when the type filter is ALL, otherwise only that type) and clears `categoryFilterId` when it becomes incompatible.

### Credit-card invoice logic

- On save, `NewTransactionUseCase` computes `invoiceMonth` (format `yyyy-MM`) for CREDIT expenses from the card's `closingDay`: purchases on or after the closing day go to next month's invoice; before it, to the current month's. `closingDay == 0` keeps the purchase in the current month.
- Non-recurring CREDIT purchases with N > 1 installments are split into **N transaction documents** (amount/N with rounding on the last installment), one per sequential `invoiceMonth`, sharing an `installmentGroupId` (UUID) and carrying `installmentNumber` (1..N). They are written atomically with a Firestore `WriteBatch` (`TransactionDao.addTransactions`).
- Recurring transactions (`isRecurring == true`) exist as a **single template document** that is projected into every month it occurs in (see "Recurring transactions" below). They are never materialized as one document per month.

### Recurring transactions

- Model: a recurring transaction is one `transactions` document with `isRecurring = true` plus recurrence control fields: `recurrenceStart` (`yyyy-MM`, first month; missing ⇒ the month of `transactionDate`, so legacy docs keep working without migration), `recurrenceEnd` (`yyyy-MM` inclusive or `null` = no end), `excludedMonths` (list of `yyyy-MM`) and `overrides` (map `yyyy-MM` → `{ amount: Double, title: String }`). Applies to recurring EXPENSE (DEBIT/CREDIT) and INCOME alike.
- Occurrence rule (`domain/model/RecurrenceRules.kt`): a recurring doc *occurs* in month `M` iff `recurrenceStart <= M <= recurrenceEnd` and `M ∉ excludedMonths`. `Transaction.occursIn(month)` / `Transaction.materializeFor(month)` implement this; the materialized copy applies the override for that month and sets `Transaction.occurrenceMonth` (the `id` stays the template id).
- Month tab: `GetTransactionsUseCase` runs the `transactionDate` range query **and** `getRecurringTransactions()`, drops recurring docs returned by the date query, and merges in the materialized occurrences for the month (`mergeWithRecurring`), so a recurring purchase registered in September also shows in October, November, … Installment docs (`installmentGroupId != null`) are also dropped from the date query and replaced by the ones whose `invoiceMonth` equals the selected month (`getTransactionsByInvoiceMonth`), so each month lists/sums only its own "Parcela X/N" instead of all N installments in the purchase month.
- Projection tab: `GetInvoiceProjectionUseCase` filters recurring docs with `occursIn(targetMonth)` and materializes them, so exclusions/overrides/end also apply to the projected invoice and recurring incomes.
- Editing/deleting a recurring occurrence from the edit dialog asks for a scope (`RecurrenceEditScope`, dialog `RecurrenceScopeDialog`): **Somente este mês** or **Este e os próximos meses** (previous months are always kept). Implemented by `UpdateRecurringOccurrenceUseCase` / `DeleteRecurringOccurrenceUseCase`:
  - Delete, this month → `excludedMonths` `arrayUnion(M)`.
  - Delete, this and future → if `M` is the start month, delete the document; otherwise `recurrenceEnd = M-1`.
  - Update, this month → `overrides[M] = {amount, title}` (nested `FieldPath`).
  - Update, this and future → if `M` is the start month, update `title`/`amount` on the template (dropping exceptions for months ≥ M); otherwise an atomic `WriteBatch` split: original gets `recurrenceEnd = M-1` and a new recurring document is created with the new values, `recurrenceStart = M`, `transactionDate` = first day of `M`, inheriting card/method/categories/type.
  - Non-recurring transactions keep the direct `UpdateTransactionUseCase`/`DeleteTransactionUseCase` flow.
  - **Categories always apply to the whole series** (template document), regardless of scope: THIS_MONTH writes the override and, when the list changed, `updateTransactionCategories` on the template; THIS_AND_FUTURE sends `category` in `updateRecurrenceTemplate`, or in the split both the original (same `WriteBatch`) and the new document receive the new list. `overrides` never carries `category`.
- `NewTransactionUseCase` sets `recurrenceStart` (month of `transactionDate`), `recurrenceEnd = null`, `excludedMonths = []`, `overrides = {}` when `isRecurring` is true; non-recurring docs leave these fields `null`.
- The month list shows "Recorrente • ajustado" when the displayed occurrence has an override.

### Financial screen

- The financial home screen (`FinancialScreen`) has two tabs (`FinancialTab.MONTH` / `FinancialTab.FILTERS`) sharing a single month selector (`selectedMonth`). Changing month (`OnPreviousMonth`/`OnNextMonth`/`OnRefresh`) calls `reloadAll()`, which fetches the month transactions (`GetTransactionsUseCase`: `transactionDate` range query merged with that month's recurring occurrences), the **open invoice shown in "Fatura por cartão"** (`loadProjection()` → `GetInvoiceProjectionUseCase` for `invoiceMonth = selectedMonth + 1`, i.e. where purchases made in the selected month land; `invoiceMonthKey`, titled "Fatura de <M+1>" in the UI; recurring docs that occur in that month are kept) and the **previous month's invoice** (`loadPaidInvoice()`: same use case for `selectedMonth - 1`, stored in `paidInvoiceTransactions`/`paidInvoiceRecurringTransactions`). Switching tabs never reloads.
  - **Mês**: detailed, unfiltered summary of the selected month computed in `FinancialUiState` — balance/income/expense, "Fatura por cartão" (`invoiceByCard`, "fecha dia X • vence dia Y", `projectedInvoiceTotal`; each row is clickable → `OnCardInvoiceClicked(cardId)` → `FinancialEffect.NavigateToCardInvoice(cardId, invoiceMonthKey)` → `card_invoice` screen), credit × debit expenses (`creditExpense`/`debitExpense`), expense nature (`recurringExpense` / `installmentExpense` / `singleExpense`), top categories (`expenseByCategory`: top `TOP_CATEGORIES` + `OTHERS_KEY`, percent over `totalExpense`; multi-category transactions count fully in each category) and `expenseByCard`. The item list is collapsed by default behind "Ver transações (N)" (`isMonthListExpanded`, `OnToggleMonthList`). Recurring CREDIT expenses join the invoice for every month, deduplicated against the `invoiceMonth` query by excluding items whose own `invoiceMonth` equals the displayed invoice month, `invoiceMonthKey` (`recurringCreditInInvoice`).
  - **Cash-balance rule**: credit purchases do **not** reduce the month balance when made; they are paid with the next month's salary. `balance = totalIncome - cashExpense`, where `cashExpense = debitExpense + paidInvoiceTotal` and `paidInvoiceTotal` is the invoice closed in `paidInvoiceMonth` (= `selectedMonth - 1`; `paidInvoiceItems` applies the same recurring-credit dedup against the M-1 key). The SummaryCard shows "Despesas" = `cashExpense` with helper lines "Débito • Fatura de MMM/yy" and "Compras no crédito do mês" (`creditExpense`). `totalExpense`/`creditExpense`/`expenseByCategory`/`expenseByCard` keep meaning "purchases dated in the month" for the breakdown sections; the Filtros tab (`filteredBalance`) is unaffected.
  - **Filtros**: analysis over the same month transactions. Filters: type (`typeFilter`), payment method (`PaymentMethodFilter` ALL/CREDIT/DEBIT — only EXPENSE items match CREDIT/DEBIT), multi-select categories (`categoryFilterIds`, OR semantics; `OnTypeFilterChanged` drops ids incompatible with the new type), card (`cardFilterId`), "Só recorrentes" (`recurringOnly`, applies to incomes too), "Só parceladas" (`installmentsOnly`: `installments > 1` or `installmentGroupId != null`) and `groupBy` (`FilterGroupBy` NONE/CATEGORY/CARD). Derived: `filteredTransactions`, `filteredIncome/Expense/Balance`, `groupedTotals` (`GroupTotal`, null key = "Sem categoria"/"Sem cartão", a transaction with N categories enters N groups), `hasActiveFilters`; `OnClearFilters` resets everything including `groupBy`. Filters are not persisted.
- Tapping a transaction (month list or filtered list) opens an edit dialog to adjust `title`/`amount`/**categories** or delete the document (`UpdateTransactionUseCase(transaction, title, amount, categoryIds)`/`DeleteTransactionUseCase`). The dialog shows `FilterChip`s for `availableCategories` filtered by the transaction's `type` (ids not in that list are dropped on confirm). For installments (`installmentGroupId != null`) a changed category list is propagated to every installment of the group via `TransactionRepository.updateCategoriesForInstallmentGroup` (`whereEqualTo("installmentGroupId")` + `WriteBatch`); title/amount stay per-installment. For recurring transactions, confirming Save/Excluir opens `RecurrenceScopeDialog` (state `FinancialUiState.pendingRecurringAction`, events `OnRecurringScopeConfirm`/`OnRecurringScopeDismiss`) to choose "Somente este mês" or "Este e os próximos meses" — see "Recurring transactions". The reference month is `Transaction.occurrenceMonth` of the clicked item (fallback: `selectedMonth`). `EditTransactionDialog`/`RecurrenceScopeDialog` and the pt-BR formatters (`formatCurrency`, `monthLabel`, `shortMonthLabel`) live in `presentation/common` (`TransactionEditDialogs.kt`, `FinancialFormatters.kt`) and are shared with the card-invoice screen.
- Card invoice screen (`presentation/screen/card_invoice/`, route `card_invoice_screen/{cardId}/{invoiceMonth}` with `invoiceMonth` = `yyyy-MM`, args read via `SavedStateHandle` keys `CardInvoiceViewModel.ARG_CARD_ID`/`ARG_INVOICE_MONTH`): bank-statement style view of one card's invoice. The ViewModel reuses `GetInvoiceProjectionUseCase(invoiceMonth)` and `CardInvoiceUiState.items` filters by `cardId` with the same recurring-credit dedup, sorted by purchase date desc with recurring items last. Header shows bank + "final NNNN", total, closing/due days and subtotals (Parceladas / À vista / Recorrentes); each installment row shows "Parcela X/N • total R$" where the total is the approximation `Transaction.installmentPurchaseTotal` (= `amount × installments`; may differ by cents since the last installment absorbs rounding). Tapping an item reuses the shared edit/recurrence-scope dialogs with the same update/delete/recurring flows as the dashboard.
- Tests for the screen live in `src/test/.../presentation/screen/financial/` (`FinancialViewModelTest`, `contract/FinancialUiStateTest`) and `.../card_invoice/` (`CardInvoiceViewModelTest`, `contract/CardInvoiceUiStateTest`); the ViewModel tests build the real use cases over `FakeTransactionRepository` plus small fakes for `CardRepository`/`CategoryTransactionRepository`. Use-case tests for the edit flow: `UpdateTransactionUseCaseTest` and `RecurringOccurrenceUseCasesTest`.
- The new-transaction screen has a **Data** field (after "Valor") that defaults to today and opens `FinancialDatePickerDialog`; any past or future date is accepted. `NewTransactionViewModel.submit()` persists `NewTransactionUiState.date` via `LocalDate.toTransactionTimestamp()` (today → current time of day, other days → local start of day). Because `NewTransactionUseCase` derives `invoiceMonth` and `recurrenceStart` from `transactionDate`, picking a date in another month moves the credit-card invoice month and the recurrence start accordingly. The `new_card` "Saldo inicial"/"Fatura atual" transactions still use `Timestamp.now()`.
- Known limitations (current behavior, not bugs to "fix" silently): `status` is always saved as `"pending"`; installment documents created before the split feature are not migrated.

## Data

- Financial data lives in Firestore collections accessed directly from the client with the authenticated user. Any new collection access must be paired with a matching rule update in `web/firestore.rules` (deployed via `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` from `web\`), otherwise reads/writes fail with `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Current rules: authenticated users can read `transactions`/`cards`/`transactions_category`; create `transactions` (requires `transactionType in ['EXPENSE','INCOME']`) and `cards`; update only `title`/`amount`/`category` of a transaction (`category` must be a list; it is replaced freely by the edit dialog and shrunk via `arrayRemove` on category deletion), plus `recurrenceEnd` (string) / `excludedMonths` (list) / `overrides` (map) when the document has `isRecurring == true`; update only `bank`/`paymentMethods`/`finalCode`/`closingDay`/`invoiceDueDate` of a card; create/update/delete `transactions_category` (`title` non-empty string, `description` string, `transactionType` in `['EXPENSE','INCOME']`); and delete `transactions`. All other client writes are denied.
- Backfill for the `transactionType` field: `web/functions/scripts/backfillTransactionType.js` sets `transactionType = "EXPENSE"` on every `transactions_category` and `transactions` document that lacks a valid value (batches of 500, Admin SDK via Application Default Credentials, project from `web/.firebaserc`). Preview with `npm --prefix web\functions run migrate:transaction-type -- --dry-run`, apply with `npm --prefix web\functions run migrate:transaction-type`. It is idempotent; run it once after deploying this feature.
